test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 16 Jun, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

'He wants something done, / and it has not happen / fast enough,' he said.
solution:
The correct answer is **option (4)**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous segment is **“and it has not happen”.**
 
• This segment is in the ***present perfect tense***. Rule (**Subject + have/has +V3**)
 
• **‘happen’ **is the base form(V1) of verb. The past participle(V3) form of the verb is **‘happened’.**
 
• Hence, it should be written as** “and it has not happened”.**
 
 
• **For example: **He has completed his task.
 
 

Therefore, the correct sentence is *“He wants something done, **and it has not happened **fast enough,” he said.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

__
 
• The phrase **"something done"** is a way of expressing that a task or action needs to be completed without specifying the exact task.
 
• It's a general term used when someone wants a particular action to be taken care of, but they may not provide all the details about what that action is.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• It is a direct speech. 
 
• It is not necessary to change the tense which is under quotation.
 
• If we change it into indirect, we have to change it into past tense.
 
• In this context, no need to change it.
